name: scrypt_alg
prose: Computes the scrypt key derivation (RFC 7914) of pass and salt with cost N, block size r and parallelism p, writing keylen bytes to key, or only validating the parameters when key is NULL. Precondition: N must be a power of two of at least 2, r and p non-zero, sha256 a fetched SHA-256 digest; maxmem is the memory limit in bytes. It returns 0 without raising an error if r or p is 0, N < 2 or N is not a power of two. It returns 0 with EVP_R_MEMORY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED if p > (2^30 - 1) / r, if 16*r is small enough and N >= 2^(16*r), if p*128*r exceeds INT_MAX, if the size of the work array 128*r*(N+2) words would overflow, or if the total memory p*128*r + 32*r*(N+2)*4 exceeds maxmem (maxmem is capped at SIZE_MAX). If key is NULL it returns 1 here, having only checked the parameters. Otherwise it allocates one buffer holding B, X, T and V (returning 0 without an error if allocation fails), derives B with one-iteration PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 from pass and salt, runs scryptROMix over each of the p blocks, and derives the output key with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 from pass and the mixed B. A failure of either PBKDF2 call raises EVP_R_PBKDF2_ERROR and returns 0. The work buffer is cleared and freed on all paths after it was allocated. Returns 1 on success.

name: ecxkem_init
prose: Initialises an X25519/X448 KEM (encapsulate or decapsulate) context. Precondition: vecxctx is a PROV_ECX_CTX; vecx is the recipient key (dereferenced without a NULL check by ecx_key_check); vauth is an optional authentication key; operation is EVP_PKEY_OP_ENCAPSULATE or EVP_PKEY_OP_DECAPSULATE. It returns 0 if the provider is not running, and 0 without changing the context if the recipient key fails the check (a key without a private part is only accepted when the operation is not decapsulation). It then replaces the context recipient key: recipient_key_set frees the old recipient key first, looks up the KEM info for the key (returning -2 if the key type has no KEM info, in which case the old key is already released and the new one not stored), sets the KDF name to HKDF, and takes a reference on the new key (returning 0 if the reference cannot be taken); a result <= 0 from this step is returned unchanged. If an authentication key vauth is given, it must match the parameters of the recipient key, must have a private part when the operation is encapsulation, and must be stored by sender_authkey_set (which also frees the old sender key and takes a reference); any of these failing returns 0 (the recipient key set earlier stays in place). Finally it records the operation in ctx->op and returns the result of ecxkem_set_ctx_params(vecxctx, params). A successful return is the result of that last call.

name: ossl_prov_drbg_instantiate
prose: Instantiates a DRBG: gathers entropy and a nonce and calls the DRBG-specific instantiate. Precondition: drbg is valid; strength must not exceed drbg->strength; pers (NULL selects the built-in personalisation string) must not be longer than drbg->max_perslen. The function returns 1 exactly when drbg->state equals EVP_RAND_STATE_READY at the end label, otherwise 0. Early failures jump to the end without changing the state: a requested strength above drbg->strength (PROV_R_INSUFFICIENT_DRBG_STRENGTH) and a too long personalisation string (PROV_R_PERSONALISATION_STRING_TOO_LONG) leave the state as it was; a state other than UNINITIALISED raises PROV_R_IN_ERROR_STATE (state ERROR) or PROV_R_ALREADY_INSTANTIATED and also leaves the state as it was, so for a DRBG that is already READY the function raises that error but still returns 1. Otherwise it sets the state to ERROR and tries to obtain a nonce when min_noncelen > 0 (from the parent nonce callback, by increasing the requested entropy when a parent exists, or from prov_drbg_get_nonce without a parent), computes the next reseed counter, obtains entropy of the required size (PROV_R_ERROR_RETRIEVING_ENTROPY on a size violation) and calls drbg->instantiate (failure raises PROV_R_ERROR_INSTANTIATING_DRBG). The entropy is cleaned up after the instantiate call, and the nonce at the end label. Only on success does it set the state to READY, generate_counter to 1, reseed_time to the current time and publish the reseed counter, so on a failure after the state was set the state stays ERROR and the reseed counter is not advanced.
note: slice shows drbg.c:349-464 (read fully; get_entropy, prov_drbg_get_nonce and drbg->instantiate not read). Original reviewer right: when the state is already READY the code goes to end (374-379) with the state READY and returns 1 (461-462). Round-15 reviewer right: the strength and personalisation failures do not touch the state, and the reseed counter is only stored on success (456).

name: ossl_prov_drbg_reseed_unlocked
prose: Reseeds a DRBG whose lock is already held by the caller. Precondition: drbg valid; ent (may be NULL) is caller-supplied entropy of ent_len bytes within the DRBG entropy length limits; adin/adinlen is optional additional input within max_adinlen. Returns 1 only if the state is READY at the end, otherwise 0. It returns 0 at once if the provider is not running. If the state is not READY it first calls rand_drbg_restart to try to recover (which may change the state); afterwards a state of ERROR raises PROV_R_IN_ERROR_STATE and a state of UNINITIALISED raises PROV_R_NOT_INSTANTIATED, both returning 0 without touching the state further. If ent is given and shorter than min_entropylen or longer than max_entropylen it raises an error, sets the state to ERROR and returns 0. A too long adin raises PROV_R_ADDITIONAL_INPUT_TOO_LONG and returns 0 (state unchanged). From then on the state is set to ERROR and only set back to READY on success. It computes the next reseed counter; if ent was given it is applied with drbg->reseed (in FIPS builds as additional input with no entropy, otherwise as entropy together with adin, after which adin is not used again), a failure raising PROV_R_UNABLE_TO_RESEED and returning 0. It then draws entropy from its own sources (a size violation raises PROV_R_ERROR_RETRIEVING_ENTROPY and goes to the end, returning 0) and reseeds with it. Only on success does it set READY, generate_counter = 1, reseed_time = now, publish the reseed counter and refresh the parent reseed counter; the temporary entropy is cleaned up at the end label.
note: slice shows drbg.c:479-584 (read fully; rand_drbg_restart, get_entropy and drbg->reseed not read). Original reviewer right: the not-instantiated case returns 0 with the state UNINITIALISED (500-503), not ERROR. Round-15 reviewer right: rand_drbg_restart (494) may change the state before the ERROR check at 496, so the state is not simply unchanged.

name: rsa_set_ctx_params
prose: Applies signature context parameters (FIPS indicators, digest and properties, padding mode, PSS salt length, MGF1 digest) to an RSA signature context. Precondition: vprsactx is a PROV_RSA_CTX; params is an OSSL_PARAM array that may be empty. Returns 0 if the context is NULL; returns 1 immediately if params is empty (no defaults are applied then). Otherwise it first processes the four FIPS indicator parameters (any failure returns 0), then reads the digest name and properties (a failed string read returns 0). The pad mode may be given as an integer or a string name; an unknown name or other type returns 0 (an unknown string leaves the current mode); OAEP padding, and PSS padding for a context that is not signing or verifying, are rejected with PROV_R_ILLEGAL_OR_UNSUPPORTED_PADDING_MODE, as are PKCS1, no-padding and X9.31 padding for non-RSA key types (X9.31 has extra FIPS checks). A PSS salt length requires PSS padding to be the selected mode (PROV_R_NOT_SUPPORTED otherwise); it may be an integer or one of the strings digest, max, auto, auto-digestmax or a decimal number; values below RSA_PSS_SALTLEN_AUTO_DIGEST_MAX give PROV_R_INVALID_SALT_LENGTH, and for a PSS-restricted key an auto salt length is only allowed when verifying and a salt length shorter than min_saltlen (or digest size shorter than it) gives PROV_R_PSS_SALTLEN_TOO_SMALL. An MGF1 digest requires PSS padding (PROV_R_INVALID_MGF1_MD otherwise). Only after all these parsing checks pass does it store saltlen and pad_mode in the context; it then defaults the digest to RSA_DEFAULT_DIGEST_NAME when PSS padding is selected and no digest is set, sets up the MGF1 digest if given (failure returns 0), and sets up the digest if one was given or defaulted (failure returns 0), otherwise it checks that the existing digest is compatible with the padding (failure returns 0). Returns 1 on success. An earlier failure leaves saltlen and pad_mode unchanged, but a later failure (MGF1 or digest setup) happens after they were stored.

Round-15 and round-17 reviewers wrong for this source: an empty params array does return 1 early (1561-1562), before any default digest is applied.

name: rsa_sign
prose: One-shot RSA signing entry point of the provider signature implementation. Precondition: vprsactx is a PROV_RSA_CTX initialised for signing; sig may be NULL to ask for the signature length; sigsize is the room in sig. It returns 0 without raising an error if the provider is not running or the context is NULL. If the context does not allow one-shot calls (flag_allow_oneshot clear, for example after a streaming update began) it raises PROV_R_ONESHOT_CALL_OUT_OF_ORDER and returns 0. For a message-signing context (EVP_PKEY_OP_SIGNMSG): with sig == NULL it only calls rsa_sign_message_final to obtain the length and does not feed tbs to the digest; otherwise it returns the logical AND of rsa_signverify_message_update(tbs, tbslen) and rsa_sign_message_final(sig, siglen, sigsize), skipping the final step if the update fails. For any other operation it returns the result of rsa_sign_directly (signing the already prepared tbs directly). The return value is that of the delegated function, or 0 for the early failures.

Original reviewer right: with sig == NULL only the final (size query) step runs, not update and final (901-902). Round-15 reviewer right: the not-running and NULL-context cases return 0 silently (889-890), only the one-shot ordering error raises an error.

name: file_set_ctx_params
prose: Applies store context parameters to a file store loader context. Precondition: loaderctx is a struct file_ctx_st (dereferenced without a NULL check); params may be empty. It returns 1 at once if params is empty. For a context that is not a directory it replaces the stored property query (OSSL_STORE_PARAM_PROPERTIES) and input type (OSSL_STORE_PARAM_INPUT_TYPE) if present: the old string is freed and set to NULL first and a failed string read returns 0 (leaving that field NULL). For a directory these two parameters are accepted but ignored. OSSL_STORE_PARAM_EXPECT is read into expected_type for every kind of context (failed read returns 0). OSSL_STORE_PARAM_SUBJECT, if present, is only allowed for directories (otherwise it raises PROV_R_SEARCH_ONLY_SUPPORTED_FOR_DIRECTORIES and returns 0); the DER-encoded name is decoded, hashed with X509_NAME_hash_ex and written as an 8-digit hexadecimal string into the directory search name; a failed octet string read or DER decode returns 0, and a hash failure returns 0 after the search name was already written. Failures other than the subject-on-file case raise no error here. Returns 1 if all present parameters were handled.

name: compute_pqueue_growth
prose: Computes a new capacity for the priority queue arrays by repeatedly multiplying current by 8/5 until it reaches target. Parameters are sizes; max_nodes (SIZE_MAX divided by the larger of the heap and element sizes) is a file-level limit. If current >= target it returns current unchanged without looping. Otherwise, while current < target: it returns 0 if current is already at or above max_nodes; it sets current to current*8/5 using the overflow-checked safe_muldiv_size_t and returns 0 if that computation reports overflow; and it clamps current to max_nodes if the product reached or exceeded it. When the loop ends it returns the resulting current, which is then at least target and at most max_nodes. So a target above max_nodes ends with 0 (after clamping, the next iteration sees current >= max_nodes), and a target at or below max_nodes returns a value between target and max_nodes. Caveat: when current is 0 and target is positive, 0*8/5 stays 0, so the loop never terminates; callers must not pass a zero current with a non-zero target.
note: ssl/priority_queue.c:86-101 read fully (slice cut the head; max_nodes definition at line 62 read; safe_muldiv_size_t not read). Round-1 reviewer right: the result is bounded by max_nodes for target > current. Round-2 reviewer right: when growth reaches max_nodes the value is clamped and returned if target <= max_nodes (97-100). Round-15 reviewer right: current == 0 with target > 0 never makes progress (94 gives 0 every time), so the loop is infinite.

name: json_undefer
prose: Emits any deferred indentation. If json->defer_indent is not set it returns without doing anything. Otherwise it calls json_indent, which clears defer_indent first (so there is no recursion) and, only in pretty-print mode, writes a newline followed by indentation of depth*4 repetitions of a four-space string, where depth is the number of open containers on the bit stack; that is 16 spaces per level, not 4. When pretty printing is off the flag is simply cleared and nothing is written. Writes go through json_write_char and json_write_str, which do nothing once the encoder is in the error state and raise the error flag if the write buffer rejects a write; json_undefer itself returns nothing.
note: json_enc.c:304-310 and json_indent 332-346 read fully. Original reviewer right: indentation is only emitted in pretty mode (338-339), otherwise the flag is cleared without output. Round-15 reviewer right: the loop at 344-345 writes a four-space string depth*4 times.

name: json_pre_item
prose: Prepares the encoder for the next value (the part that writes separators before an item). Returns 0 without raising a new error if the encoder is already in the error state. State PRE_COMMA: it looks at the top of the container stack: if the top is an object (value 0) it raises the error flag and returns 0 (a value was given where a key was expected); if the top is an array (value 1) it writes a comma, returns 0 if that write failed, and then calls json_indent; if the stack is empty (negative result) and sequence mode is on it writes the 0x1E record separator (a write failure here is not checked, so the function can still return 1 after a write error); then the state becomes PRE_ITEM. State PRE_ITEM: nothing to do. State PRE_KEY or any other value: it raises the error flag and returns 0. Returns 1 when the encoder is ready for the item, including when the container stack is empty.

Original reviewer right: already-in-error returns 0 without raising (352-353) and the 0x1E write at 372-373 is not checked before return 1. Round-15 reviewer right: the error is raised when the top is an object (s == 0, 359-362), while an empty stack proceeds.

name: composite_end
prose: Closes an object (type 0, char }) or an array (type 1, char ]). Returns without doing anything if the encoder is already in the error state. It clears defer_indent (remembering the old value), then raises the error flag and returns if the container on top of the stack is not of the requested type or the stack is empty (peek differs from type), or if closing an object while the state is PRE_ITEM, i.e. a key has been written but its value is still pending; closing an empty object (state PRE_KEY or PRE_COMMA) is allowed. It then pops the stack (failure raises the error flag and returns), writes an indentation only if the opening bracket was not followed directly by this close (was_defer clear), writes the closing character and runs json_post_item, which sets the state to PRE_COMMA and, for an outermost value in sequence mode, writes a newline. The character writes can themselves raise the error flag.
note: json_enc.c:420-449 read fully (json_pop and json_indent not read in detail). Original reviewer right: it returns silently when already in error (424-425) and a failed write also raises the error flag through json_write_char. Round-15 reviewer right: the pending-key error is only for objects in PRE_ITEM state (434-437); an empty object is fine.

name: ossl_json_key
prose: Writes an object key. Returns without doing anything if the encoder is already in the error state. It raises the error flag and returns if the top of the container stack is not an object (peek != 0, including an empty stack). If the state is PRE_COMMA (a previous member was written) it writes a comma and moves the state to PRE_KEY. It then writes the indentation (json_indent, which only emits output in pretty mode) and, if the state is not PRE_KEY at that point (for example a key was already written and its value is pending), it raises the error flag and returns. Otherwise it writes the key as a quoted string, then a colon (followed by a space in pretty mode) unless a write error occurred, and sets the state to PRE_ITEM, awaiting the value. It returns nothing; failures are recorded in the encoder error flag.
note: json_enc.c:481-512 read fully (json_write_qstring not read). Original reviewer right: after the key is written the state becomes STATE_PRE_ITEM (511). Round-15 reviewer right: the error path when the state is not PRE_KEY after the indent (498-501) was missing.
